title: A Security-Review Waiver Granted Before the Waiver Rule Ended
scenario_text:
A procurement analyst at Quorn Systems must decide whether a new SaaS vendor's security review can be waived, given how a comparable vendor was handled last year.

**Decision A (2023-10)**
Vendor 'Blackwood Analytics' | SaaS tool handling customer PII | held a current SOC 2 Type II report. Procurement WAIVED the full internal security review. Note: 'Per policy at the time, vendors handling PII with a valid SOC 2 Type II may have the internal security review waived.'

**Current request C (2024-06-05)**
Vendor 'Fenwick Data' | new SaaS tool that will process customer PII | holds a current SOC 2 Type II report. The requesting team wants onboarding completed this week.

**Vendor Security Policy (current, effective 2024-02-15)**
All new SaaS vendors that will handle customer PII MUST complete a full internal security review before onboarding. SOC 2 Type II reports are accepted as supporting evidence within that review but no longer qualify a vendor for a waiver. The SOC 2-based waiver that existed previously was eliminated when this policy took effect.

**Slack — #procurement**
Requester: 'We waived the review for Blackwood last year because they had SOC 2. Fenwick has SOC 2 too, so waive it and let's move.'
Analyst: 'Blackwood was waived back in October — that was before the February security policy. Let me confirm whether waivers even exist anymore.'

The requester is under a deadline and is treating the Blackwood waiver as a repeatable shortcut. No full security review has been started for Fenwick.
question: Can procurement waive the full internal security review for Fenwick Data based on its SOC 2 Type II report? Answer Yes or No.
